recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is; no follow-up source work is needed for FHIR-44719 unless a future FHIRPath decision changes primitive-with-extension empty() semantics.
issue_request: FHIR-44719 was an Applied/Persuasive FHIR-I R6 change request asking to clarify that empty() considers extensions by adding an example where Patient.active has no primitive value but has extensions.
initial_application: Source commit 5465375c661b23de9bfabd4c18a30b9e51af4443, titled 'FHIR-44719 Clarify that empty() considers extensions', added the Patient.active.hasValue()/empty() example to source/fhirpath.html.
additional_context: The originating Zulip thread records Grahame Grieve's answer that such an element should not be empty, and FHIR-I minutes for 2025-01-06 record the 10-0-0 Persuasive vote. Later commit 4961dcb9df16e3e7316d64a1062c5f5c5c7701d4 changed the example's operator from && to the FHIRPath keyword and without changing the approved meaning.
reconciliation: No source edit was made. The combined branch already contains source/fhirpath.html text stating that primitive-extension expressions are not mutually exclusive and includes '!Patient.active.hasValue() and !Patient.active.empty()' as an example that can be true when extensions are present but no value is present.

related_jiras.note: Later edited the same example from && to FHIRPath and syntax, preserving the FHIR-44719 clarification.
Added other examples to the same FHIRPath page shortly after FHIR-44719 but did not alter this issue's required clarification.
